dirt_product_evidence: 1964 custom fuzz boxes; Octavia; later Page 1/Classic Fuzz
builder_evidence: Mayer states he designed and made his first fuzz guitar effects pedal in 1964 and describes making fuzz boxes for Jimmy Page, Jeff Beck and other musicians; Fuzzboxes documents his 1966 public fuzz-box advertisement and later small-run effects work.
relationship_status: Commercial chronology and later corporate production are separate from his early custom work; preserve Roger Mayer as the maker of the documented custom fuzz/Octavia lineage.
recommended_treatment: Builder census eligible, with entity type Custom / historical micro-builder rather than mass-production manufacturer.

builder_evidence: Rock & Roll Hall of Fame material identifies the custom fuzz used by The Ventures as built by Red Rhodes; historical fuzz references document that Rhodes made several fuzz boxes for fellow musicians rather than a mass-market production line.
relationship_status: The Rhodes fuzz was never a general commercial pedal line. Award/Mosrite amplifier relationships and later circuit-attribution debates remain separate research questions.
recommended_treatment: Builder census eligible, but classify as Custom / historical micro-builder and not a conventional commercial pedal manufacturer.

dirt_product_evidence: Homemade fuzz box for Jeff Beck at Eel Pie Island
builder_evidence: Paul Lucas states he designed and constructed the first fuzz box Jeff Beck played through at Eel Pie Island in 1964, using a passive mixer box and transistor amplifier.
relationship_status: This is a one-off/custom device rather than an established pedal company. It qualifies the maker as a historical custom builder but should remain distinct from commercial builder records.
recommended_treatment: Keep as a research-only custom-builder node until the archive establishes a policy for individual one-off makers in the public census.

builder_evidence: Fuzzboxes documents a 1966 Kelly Fuzz Box advertisement and testimony suggesting Kelly may have made it, but the surviving evidence explicitly leaves open whether the fuzz was Kelly-built or a Macari/Sola Sound rebrand. No surviving example is known.
relationship_status: Possible Macari/Sola Sound relationship is unresolved.
recommended_treatment: Retain as provisional research-only; do not promote to verified builder until physical manufacture is better established.

builder_evidence: Fuzzboxes says Pepe Rush initially built the Pep Box and later partnered with Charlie Watkins; WEM eventually took over production. This is strong evidence for WEM as a manufacturer of a dirt product, but WEM is already canonical in the archive.
relationship_status: Do not create a separate Watkins builder node solely from the WEM production transition.
recommended_treatment: Cross-reference existing WEM builder record and preserve Watkins as a company/person relationship within that lineage.
